general_information.Description: - Main objective: This course aims to equip students with practical operational skills to plan, implement and supervise food and beverage services, manage key resources, and apply standard operating procedures to deliver safe, efficient and guest‑oriented F&B operations in hospitality settings. - Description: This course examines the managerial and supervisory functions within F&B departments, including menu and service concepts, basic production and service workflows, cost and inventory control, quality, safety and hygiene, and the coordination of front‑ and back‑of‑house activities to meet financial, managerial and guest satisfaction objectives. Students are also expected to utilize contemporary AI tools (namely Gemini, ChatGPT or Copilot) to support industry research, scenario analysis, and the development of concept visuality or practical tasks in a responsible and ethical manner. -Teaching method: Through lecture, hands-on practice, roleplay, case studies, and simulated operational scenarios. - Facility and equipment requirement : Depending on the training condition of each campus, the course will be implemented in school lab designed up to 4-5* hotel standard, real hotel or other places, which fully met with requirements.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are required to attend with professional grooming standards. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time. - Students are encouraged to use laptop in class only for learning purpose as well as comply with the time and regulation.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Explain key sectors, structures, functions, and stages of food and beverage operations, and outline key factors of meal experience and customer service.
Demonstrate professional attributes, technical skills, service conventions, and interpersonal behaviours, including teamwork, discipline, and communication in F&B settings.
Apply health, safety, and security protocols, and optimize service areas, serviceware for efficient F&B operations.
Describe food production and service methods, demonstrate knowledge of foods, beverages, menu types, basic menu development, and key characteristics of different service styles.
Execute standard operating procedures for different service styles and events, following appropriate service sequences in front‑ and back‑of‑house operations.
Apply basic F&B supervisory knowledge in legal control, sales, pricing, staffing, and performance measures to support operational and financial objectives.

assessments.CLO: CLO1, CLO2, CLO3, CLO4, CLO5, CLO6
assessments.No Question: Maximum length of the group assignment should be 10 pages maximum excluding appendices.
assessments.Grading Guide: Presentation in class and submission via email or anycourse supporting platfrom
assessments.Note: - Four or five students per group. - Students are required to develop a restaurant concept, with clear elaboration/demonstration of the service style, production methods, menu, floor plan, equipment & furniture, staffing, etc. Students must also submit a teaser video that could generally visualize the concept and highlight what are signatures of the restaurant. - Groups and groups ideas are determined on the third session of the course. Work will be break down into stages and examined during the course. Final work to be submitted prior to the presentation of the topic.All assignments should be typed and double-spaced with 11-point font, and must be submitted in both soft and hard copy. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission - Evaluation will be based on both presentation, teaser video and written report (recommended 20%, 10%, 70% accordingly)

assessments.Grading Guide: With Lab's facilities. Students have 1 week to practice in group since the Practical session.
assessments.Note: - Students are assessed in group of four or five. - The test is conducted in 6 sessions (2 new slots). - Students are randomly assigned different restaurant concepts/ types of menus/ courses that required different types of tablewares. - Each group member plays a role in a restaurant: host, waiter, runner, busser. - They need to deliver the meal smoothly with harmonious team collaboration.

assessments.Grading Guide: With Lab's facilities. Students have 1 week to practice since the Practical session.
assessments.Note: - The test is conducted in 6 sessions (2 new slots). - Equipment knowledge can be assessed based on table setting activities. - Menu knowledge: 3 menus & 3 guest characteristics are provided prior to Testing day. During the Test, each student draws 1 menu and 1 guest persona, then perform the role of a waiter/waitress consulting the menu according to guest's preferences. - Students are encouraged to utilize AI to practice their interaction with guest at home, by inputting different scenarios given in advance. - The role of guest could be played by lecturer or a student.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on topics of studied units
assessments.Grading Guide: Attendance: FAP's attendance report Class participation: teacher's records
assessments.Note: Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots Attendance check at any time during course

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 1-The foodservice industry
constructive_questions.Details: How have changes in consumer lifestyles and global trends influenced the development of the modern food and beverage industry?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 1-The foodservice industry
constructive_questions.Details: Why do people choose to eat outside their homes, and how do you think F&B businesses adapt to different customer needs and occasions?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 1-The foodservice industry
constructive_questions.Details: In what ways do the meal experience and customer expectations vary across different types of foodservice businesses (e.g., café, hotel restaurant vs. cafeteria)?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 2-Staff attributes, skills and knowledge
constructive_questions.Details: If you were recruiting staff for a fine-dining restaurant versus a casual café, which attributes and skills would you prioritize, and why?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 2-Staff attributes, skills and knowledge
constructive_questions.Details: Describe a scenario where strong interpersonal skills can resolve a critical service issue in F&B operations.

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 2-Staff attributes, skills and knowledge
constructive_questions.Details: Why is adherence to key service conventions essential for both guest satisfaction and operational efficiency in F&B establishments?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 3-Food and beverage service areas and equipment
constructive_questions.Details: How would you design an efficient service area for a high-volume banquet? What equipment and layout choices would you prioritize?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 3-Food and beverage service areas and equipment
constructive_questions.Details: What factors should be considered when selecting tableware and glassware for a new food and beverage outlet?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 3-Food and beverage service areas and equipment
constructive_questions.Details: How does technology integration (e.g., POS, smart equipment) change the operation of modern F&B service areas?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 4-The menu, menu knowledge and accompaniments
constructive_questions.Details: How do local culture and customer demographics influence menu design for a new restaurant?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 4-The menu, menu knowledge and accompaniments
constructive_questions.Details: Imagine you are launching a menu for a themed event. What steps would you take to ensure the menu sequence and accompaniments create a cohesive guest experience?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 4-The menu, menu knowledge and accompaniments
constructive_questions.Details: What is the impact of proper menu knowledge on upselling and overall revenue in food and beverage businesses?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 5-Beverages - non-alcoholic and alcoholic
constructive_questions.Details: What are some trends and regulations for F&B businesses who are selling alcohol beverages in Vietnam, and how do F&B outlets respond?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 5-Beverages - non-alcoholic and alcoholic
constructive_questions.Details: What safety and service considerations must be observed when offering a diverse selection of alcoholic beverages?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 5-Beverages - non-alcoholic and alcoholic
constructive_questions.Details: How can a staff use beverage knowledge to enhance both guest satisfaction and business profitability?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 6-The service sequence (table service)
constructive_questions.Details: Imagine a busy dinner service: how would you ensure the smooth coordination of all steps in the classic table service sequence?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 6-The service sequence (table service)
constructive_questions.Details: What challenges might arise when shifting from traditional silver service to more contemporary table service styles in a modern restaurant?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 10-Enhanced service techniques
constructive_questions.Details: How can the implementation of tableside service techniques (e.g., flambé, carving) enhance the guest experience and restaurant branding?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 10-Enhanced service techniques
constructive_questions.Details: When is it appropriate to use enhanced service methods, and what training is essential to perform these techniques effectively?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 7-The service sequence (self-service, assisted service and single point service)
constructive_questions.Details: What factors determine the choice between self-service, assisted service, and single point service models in various food and beverage contexts?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 7-The service sequence (self-service, assisted service and single point service)
constructive_questions.Details: How might self-service systems be optimized to maintain both speed and quality in a busy food court scenario?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 8-The service of breakfast and afternoon tea
constructive_questions.Details: Research and present different breakfast or afternoon tea service styles in different hospitality cultures.

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 8-The service of breakfast and afternoon tea
constructive_questions.Details: What are the key elements of timing and coordination required for successful breakfast or tea service?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 9-Specialized forms of service
constructive_questions.Details: How do specialized service forms (e.g., in-room dining, airline catering) require adaptation of traditional F&B procedures?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 9-Specialized forms of service
constructive_questions.Details: What innovations in specialized service forms can you propose to improve customer experience in non-traditional settings?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 11-Event
constructive_questions.Details: Think of a successful event (wedding, banquet, or conference) you have attended. What details in food, service, and organization made it memorable, and why?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 11-Event
constructive_questions.Details: How would you plan the staffing and preparation differently for a banquet with a formal plated meal versus a large buffet reception?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 11-Event
constructive_questions.Details: How does the role of communication and coordination between event service staff, kitchen, and sales affect the guest experience during a large-scale function?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 12-Supervisory aspects of food and beverage service
constructive_questions.Details: When facing a decline in guest satisfaction scores, what managerial interventions would you prioritize to restore service quality?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 12-Supervisory aspects of food and beverage service
constructive_questions.Details: Imagine you have just been promoted to F&B supervisor. What new responsibilities and challenges would you expect to face, and what strategies would you use to motivate and train your team effectively?

constructive_questions.Name: Chapter 12-Supervisory aspects of food and beverage service
constructive_questions.Details: How does the legal environment (e.g., health, safety, licensing) shape the day-to-day responsibilities of F&B supervisors?

constructive_questions.Details: Imagine a situation where food and beverage costs unexpectedly increase. How would you use revenue and cost control tools to protect profitability?
